name: AIG_5_Human_Factors__Explainability__and_Human_Oversight
title: AIG.5 Human Factors, Explainability, and Human Oversight (Function)
description: This category is about what the consumer can see, correct, question, and override. It covers review and escalation pathways before high-impact or irreversible actions, correction of faulty input data, and explanation at a level appropriate to the consumer and the risk of the intended use.

statement.label: AIG.5#01
statement.requirement: IF an AI function can influence a high-impact health, safety, access, or financial decision THEN the system SHALL provide a risk-appropriate human or consumer review, correction, override, or escalation pathway before an irreversible or high-impact action is taken, unless a documented exception is required for immediate safety and is permitted by applicable rules.

statement.label: AIG.5#02
statement.requirement: IF the system uses AI functionality THEN the system SHALL enable a consumer to view or correct material input data that the consumer provided or that the system attributes to the consumer when incorrect input could materially affect the AI output.

statement.label: AIG.5#03
statement.requirement: IF the system displays AI output THEN the system SHOULD provide a meaningful explanation of the primary factors, data limitations, or evidence sources relevant to the output, at a level appropriate to the consumer and the risk of the intended use.

statement.label: AIG.5#04
statement.requirement: IF the system uses AI functionality THEN the system MAY offer alternative explanation formats, such as plain-language summaries, detailed technical explanations, visual context, or translated content.
